Todd Chrisley isn't letting online critics have the last word about his daughter Savannah's marriage — and his mother, Nanny Faye, had a rather cheeky take on the whole controversy.

Savannah, 29, has faced accusations of being a “gold digger” since news broke that she secretly married businessman Jason Galanis, 56, and is expecting their first child together. 

Their 27-year age gap has also fueled plenty of online chatter.

Read More: Savannah Chrisley's dad Todd claims he will never 'forget' them after prison release

But Jason's financial history has added another layer to the debate. He served federal prison time in 2020 after being linked to multimillion-dollar securities fraud schemes. 

President Donald Trump commuted his sentence in March 2025.

During an October 30 episode of his Two Sons and Me podcast, Todd, 57, pushed back against the claims about his daughter.

"There were comments today in the press about Savannah's ring, the size of it, that she is engaged to a billionaire because she's a gold digger," he said.

Nanny Faye wasn't exactly scandalized by the accusation.

"Oh, good. I don't blame her. I'd dig, too. If I knew one and I stood a chance like her, I'd be digging 24/7, till I got him," she joked.

Todd laughed before adding his own punchline, saying that if Savannah really were a gold digger, "it would have helped out if she would have started digging when I was paying all these legal fees."

He then argued that critics were overlooking Savannah's own business success, pointing to her clothing line, cosmetics and Good Girl RX.

Read More: Savannah Chrisley's mystery fiancé revealed after pregnancy news

"What do they think this girl has done her whole life, from the time that the cameras started rolling? What do they think she did with her clothing line, with her cosmetics, that she didn't make money? What do they think about Good Girl RX? How do they think this woman lives?" he asked.

headline: SSGC announces new gas supply schedule for winter
subheadline: Gas supply to domestic consumers to be prioritised during three designated cooking periods
author: Web Desk
article_text:
SSGC announces three daily gas supply slots during winter.
SNGPL imposes gas load management across Islamabad, Punjab, KP.
SNGPL gas supply to CNG and industrial sectors reduced.

The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has announced designated timings for gas availability to domestic consumers during the winter season, saying it is committed to ensuring supplies during household cooking hours in line with government instructions.

According to an announcement shared by the gas utility, domestic consumers will receive gas during three periods each day, from 6:30am to 9am, 12pm to 2:30pm and 6pm to 9pm.

The company said prioritising domestic consumers and ensuring gas availability during the specified cooking hours were part of its strategy for the winter season.

SSGC said the measures were being taken in accordance with the federal government's directives, with household consumers' convenience remaining a priority.

Gas supply restricted to cooking hours in Punjab, KP

Separately, Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) has introduced gas load management for domestic consumers in Islamabad, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, restricting supplies to three daily cooking-time slots from Wednesday as dwindling liquefied natural gas (LNG) availability and rising winter demand put further pressure on the country's gas supply system, The News reported.

Under the schedule, households will receive gas from 6:30am to 9am, noon to 2:30pm and 6pm to 9pm. The restrictions also cover Islamabad, with the government prioritising domestic consumption over other sectors to manage available supplies during the winter season.

SNGPL has also reduced gas supplies to the compressed natural gas (CNG) sector from 50 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) to 35 mmcfd, with plans to suspend supplies to the sector altogether in the coming days.

The cement industry has already switched to coal, while industrial consumers connected to the distribution network are also facing reduced gas supplies.

Industries connected directly to the transmission network, including both export-oriented and non-export industries, are currently receiving around 200 mmcfd. However, further reductions in supplies remain possible.

Meanwhile, the power sector is receiving approximately 140 mmcfd of gas, while the fertiliser industry is being supplied around 53 mmcfd..

headline: Beatrice, Eugenie forced to take difficult step before Andrew's crucial testimony
subheadline: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor faces fresh orders to appear in court as daughters make decisive move
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie were only beginning to have some semblance of normalcy in their family dynamics, when they were hit with a major setback.

The York sisters, who were recently seen with their mother Sarah Ferguson for a sombre service in UK, now face an important decision as their disgraced father is set to appear in court – but not for the Epstein scandal.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been served with a summons which will see him giving evidence in a fraud trial in the High Court around 15 December.

READ MORE: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor 'reacts' to Sarah Ferguson's bold statement

Even though, the trial will see Andrew as a witness, he could face tough questions about his financial arrangements as it is said that he was in receipt of some of the disputed payments, including a transfer to him of £750,000, via the BBC.

Since the trial is around December, this also means that the royal Christmas will once again find itself in the shadow of the Epstein scandal.

According to royal expert, Chris Riches, Beatrice and Eugenie would have been “eager” to take their families to their former Windsor home, but now they are split over whom to show their loyalties.

Last year, they both attended the Sandringham walkabout, but this time, they have a difficult choice for Christmas.

“This year they must feel under huge pressure not to snub both parents again,” he wrote in Express UK.

“If they shun them both, they will be panicking about their parents’ mental health. After what they have suffered in 2026, both Andrew and Fergie will be desperate to spend some downtime with their grandchildren.”

Moreover, the media spotlight would not help. It is a tough choice and only time will tell where Beatrice and Eugenie decide to land.

READ MORE: Andrew's court shock: Potential testimony dates released

headline: Miranda Kerr gets honest about returning to VS runway
subheadline: Miranda Kerr talks about turning down the Victoria Secret's return
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Miranda Kerr was invited to relive her Victoria’s Secret runway days, but the supermodel ultimately decided that some memories are better left in the past — especially when they involve walking in lingerie in front of a crowd.

The 43-year-old revealed on the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast, in an episode released November 3, that she was asked to return for the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show.

Although she was tempted by the opportunity, the idea of stepping back onto the runway left her feeling unexpectedly anxious.

Read More: Miranda Kerr reveals relationship status with ex Orlando Bloom

“I was really, seriously considering it,” Kerr said, recalling the “fun” memories from her six previous appearances.

“I got really excited, but then I got kind of anxious… I was meditating and fell into how I’m actually going to feel when I’m up there in my underwear.”

She continued, “Everyone’s in their underwear. I’m 43. I have four boys. I got this knot in my stomach and as much as I try to meditate and ease it, it was still there.”

Eventually, Kerr decided to listen to her instincts. “The only way I could resolve that is to say, ‘You’re not going to do the show.’ How do you feel now?”

The decision brought her relief, and she said the “knot” in her stomach disappeared once she chose not to participate.

Still, the model was grateful for the invitation, calling it an “honour” to be considered for a return at 43 and as a mother of four.

Kerr shares Flynn, 15, Hart, 7, Myles, 6, and Pierre, 2.

headline: Meghan Markle puts aside father's scandal with exciting announcement
subheadline: Duchess of Sussex starts fresh chapter after painful ordeal with Thomas Markle Sr allegations and Palace reaction
author: A. Akmal
article_text:
Meghan Markle, after undergoing emotional turmoil as her father Thomas Markle Sr is being investigated for paedophilia and child abuse allegations, is taking a step forward in life.

Prince Harry had reportedly whisked his wife and two children on holiday overseas as they dealt with the onslaught of the disturbing revelations that emerged.

However, as the Sussexes return to the UK, following their relocation into their new Cotswold home, Meghan is putting her focus back into work, especially As Ever.

READ MORE: Meghan Markle's ‘painful' struggle revealed amid father's police probe

She shared some exciting news for fans as there is a new product being added to the collection.

“A little taste of the holidays is on its way,” the announcement read. “Something sweet is coming to the As ever pantry 11.5.”

The news follows the update in the Thomas Markle Sr case where the 82-year-old has been enrolled into a dementia centre, which spells bad news for the ongoing probe.

Legal experts have stated that Thomas Sr cannot be question or tried to the claims if he is not medically fit to recall his memory. His testimony would be rendered invalid.

Meanwhile, King Charles and Prince William are secretly being kept up to date with the case, despite Palace sources stating that it is a matter of the Sussex household.

READ MORE: Prince Harry, Meghan welcome major life change in UK amid tough phase

headline: Raphinha says it was hard to play after De Miguel's death: It could have been me'
subheadline: 'It’s very difficult to go out and play a game in these circumstances. He was a player who was the same age as me' said Raphinha
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Barcelona forward Raphinha has reflected on the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel, saying it was hard for him to play Tuesday’s UEFA Championship game against Aston Villa.

De Miguel died in hospital a day after he suffered a cardiac arrest following an on-filed collision with Real Oviedo goalkeeper Jesús Owono on Monday, November 2, 2026.

He was 30.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced a three-day mourning for late De Miguel.

Raphinha netted twice as Barça beat Premier League side Villa 3-0 at Spotify Camp Nou.

“Wherever (De Miguel) is, I hope he finds his way,” Raphinha told Movistar after the game.

“I want to send his family strength… and today, not talk about football.”

“After I saw the news, I didn’t feel good. In the end, he was a fellow football player. This could have happened to any of us. It could have happened to me.”

“It’s very difficult to go out and play a game in these circumstances. He was a player who was the same age as me. Maybe that’s why it affected me so much.”

As a mark of respect, the Champions League hymn was not played before kickoff at Camp Nou, with a minute’s silence held for De Miguel instead.

Raphinha managed to continue his incredible form at the start of the season, scoring twice after Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring sheet as Barça ended Villa’s perfect start in the Champions League this season.

Raphinha, playing as a striker, netted 19 goals in all competitions this season, the most in Europe’s top five leagues.

headline: King Charles given security warning after police shock update
subheadline: Royal family's upcoming key event hits with major setback
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles received an alarming security update after the Metropolitan Police decided to reduce its presence at key royal events.

According to The Telegraph, the police force will reduce its presence at military ceremonies, including Trooping the Colour, due to budget cuts.

The annual public celebration of the British monarch's birthday takes place in London in June.

READ MORE: Harriet Phillips 'pinch-me' moment with King Charles, Queen Camilla

According to Metropolitan Police, "The public rightly want to see officers on the front line, arresting criminals and keeping our city safe. That’s our priority.

"Against a backdrop of financial cuts and increased demand, we had to make difficult decisions about what to prioritise to protect Londoners and over recent months have engaged with the Ministry of Defence around proposed changes to how we support military ceremonial events."

In the past year's ceremonial military events, 17,800 officers have been deployed, costing an estimated $14 million. Now, a private contractor will fulfil this responsibility.

READ MORE: King Charles' health concerns put William, Catherine's key plans on hold

But the decision raised security concerns, as a source from the army believes that the private security will not "provide the same level of assurance to the soldiers and the public about safety in the face of any potential security risk."

headline: Blake Lively's first appearance after lawsuit sparks online backlash
subheadline: Blake Lively's night out sparks fresh debate among fans
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Blake Lively brought vintage Chanel glamour to New York City, but her latest night out quickly became a talking point for reasons beyond her outfit.

The Gossip Girl star attended jewelry designer Brent Neale’s holiday capsule collection launch on November 3, marking what appeared to be her first official event since parting ways with longtime publicist Leslie Sloane in September.

Lively wore a navy sequin mini dress from Chanel’s Fall/Winter 1994 collection and attended alongside friends.

Read More: Blake Lively, Ryan Reynolds ‘fuming' over Justin Baldoni's career milestone

The actress has supported Neale’s designs before, even wearing the jeweler’s pieces in her 2024 film It Ends With Us.

Photos from the evening spread across social media, where reactions were decidedly mixed.

Some fans couldn't get enough of her look, with one writing, "She is beautiful." Another admitted, "Have to admit – she's gorgeous… really stunning outfit."

But others weren't convinced the appearance was simply a casual night out.

One critic questioned the timing, commenting, "Does anybody fall for these overused PR stunts anymore? What's the point?" Another added, "Her new PR need to put in some hours."

The group accompanying Lively also became a target of online commentary, with users asking, "What friends?" and "Didn't realize she had any friends."

Some commenters also brought up her ongoing legal dispute with Justin Baldoni, adding another layer to the social media debate. However, there is no evidence that the event was arranged as a publicity stunt.

Read More: Blake Lively faces painful Hollywood reality after her major fallout

Neither Lively nor her representatives have addressed the speculation.

For now, her vintage dress may have won fashion points, but the internet clearly had plenty more to discuss.

headline: Princess Andre makes bold move to rival Kylie Jenner with latest business venture
subheadline: Katie Price has been working alongside the creative team and she has even taken full interest in styling the collection herself
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Princess Andre has vowed to achieve even greater success by launching her own clothing line after previously expressing her to become the 'British Kylie Jenner.'

The 19-year-old influencer, has now announced that she is expanding her business empire with the launch of her leisurewear brand KAIIA.

The daughter of Katie Price and Peter Andre has been working alongside the creative team and she has even taken full interest in styling the collection herself.

READ MORE: 'Celebrity Race Across' first trailer features Princess, Junior Andre in daring stunt

Qasim Akhlaq, CEO of KAIIA, said: 'The photoshoot was a brilliant experience for Princess. 'She felt like she was making a music video rather than doing a traditional fashion shoot, with all the dramatic lighting, different outfits and movement. She absolutely loved it.'

'Princess is really excited about her first edit. She's had a big say in choosing the pieces and can't wait for everyone to see what she's been working on.'

The collection will be available for exclusive 24-hour early access on 9 November to customers who sign up to the KAIIA newsletter and download the app, ahead of its public launch at 10am on 10 November 2026.

Ahead of the collection's official release, Princess will host a special fan meet-and-greet at Footasylum in London on Tuesday, giving shoppers the opportunity to meet her and pose for snaps.

Princess has has already made a name of herself in the UK, particularly through her reality show, The Princess Diaries, and her social media work.

However, it has now been reported that Princess has set her sights on conquering the US market next year.

Over the weekend, a source revealed that she wants to take her cosmetics brand, By Princess, to America and give billionaire Kylie, 29, a run for her money.

READ MORE: Iconic story behind Kylie Jenner's $50 million look

headline: Meghan Markle's befitting response to critics after ‘disgusting' attacks
subheadline: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle take stern step moving forward in UK after 'painful' ordeal
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle is understood to be left taken aback by the reaction she has received in light of the scandal surrounding her father Thomas Markle Sr.

The Duchess of Sussex had made it clear that her grievances were for the victims and she was disturbed by what her father had allegedly done.

However, it believed that the reaction from the British public has been quite hypocritical especially as the royals are embroiled in a similar scandal.

READ MORE: Meghan Markle puts aside father's scandal with exciting announcement

When the allegations against Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had emerged, the larger opinion had been to not punish Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie for their parents’ mistakes.

But the views are quite different in Meghan’s case, as she is being cast as a villain in the situation. It has left Harry and Meghan “disgusted”, a source cited by Heat World said.

“Meghan’s spent years being vilified for turning her back on her father,” the insider explained.

“But now the allegations are out in the open, and it’s clear why she did that; instead of admitting their mistake, the trolls are doubling down on Meghan being the villain.”

Moreover, these are not just anonymous people online but there are people with huge platforms, which is “very damaging”. They are surprised that these people have not shown a “shred of humanity”.

Amid this time, Meghan is “tuning out the noise” as a response and she is getting all the support from her close circle especially Prince Harry.

READ MORE: Beatrice, Eugenie forced to take difficult step before Andrew's crucial testimony

headline: Hailey Bieber opens up about intense emotional changes after motherhood
subheadline: Hailey Bieber says postpartum PMDD made her feel less alone
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Hailey Bieber has shared a side of motherhood that doesn't always make it into the picture-perfect Instagram posts.

The Rhode founder revealed that she struggled with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) after welcoming her son, Jack Blues.

Speaking to Women’s Wear Daily in an interview published October 30, the 29-year-old said becoming a mother made her more aware of how much women's bodies go through during pregnancy, childbirth and beyond.

Read More: Hailey Bieber reveals future family plans with Justin Bieber

“Especially after having my own child,” she said.

“That was just a really intense and special journey that I had. There’s so much that happens when you are pregnant, during childbirth. There’s so many things that happen leading up to having a child.”

Her experience didn't end after delivery. Bieber said she struggled with PMDD postpartum and believes more conversations are needed around conditions that often go unrecognised.

“After I had my son, I struggled with that a bit, and there’s just not a lot of conversation or research around it,” she explained.

She added, “Conversation, for me personally, makes me feel less alone.”

Bieber previously discussed her diagnosis on the SHE MD podcast, revealing she was diagnosed around six months after giving birth.

She described the emotional symptoms as far more intense than the PMS she had experienced before pregnancy.

“I was like, ‘This just feels way more intense than before,’ like the lead-up to getting your period,” she recalled.

PMDD can cause severe mood changes, anxiety and depression in the days before menstruation, with symptoms often easing once a period begins.

Bieber and husband Justin welcomed Jack on August 22, 2024.

Read More: Hailey Bieber shares hilarious meme featuring Justin Bieber

Despite the challenges, she has described motherhood as something she always wanted.

“It is so fun. I always knew I wanted kids; I always wanted to be a mom,” she previously said.

headline: Nasa's Swift satellite telescope heads for fiery re-entry 22 years after launch
subheadline: Nasa's Swift satellite studies gamma-ray bursts and cosmic phenomena using three telescopes
author: Reuters
article_text:
An ageing Nasa satellite telescope that a robotic spacecraft was sent to retrieve on a failed rescue mission this summer was headed for a fiery re-entry into Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday, nearly 22 years after it was launched into orbit.

The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, weighing roughly 3,200 pounds (1,452 kg), was set to tumble out of orbit and burn up in the atmosphere somewhere over the tropics, with fragments surviving re-entry unlikely to threaten populated areas, according to Nasa.

The US Space Force has put the odds of harm coming to anyone on Earth at one chance in 2,100, Nasa said in an online statement, projecting the time of re-entry at approximately 3:30am EST (0830 GMT). The Aerospace Corporation, a nonprofit national security research entity, projected a re-entry window of 5:19am EST, plus or minus two hours.

London-based astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, an honorary professor at the Durham University Space Research Centre, cited revised US Space Force data predicting re-entry most likely to come around 7:45am EST.

"The satellite is in a very circular orbit, skimming the top of the atmosphere," he told Reuters by phone on Tuesday night. "The question is at what point does it heat up enough that it starts breaking up."

Nasa's prized $500 million Swift satellite, a first-of-its-kind multi-wavelength space observatory, has been studying gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena since 2004, using its array of three telescopes.

The observatory, which has no onboard propulsion system of its own, has been drifting toward an expected demise for months as it circles the globe at a speed of roughly 17,000 miles per hour (27,359 kph).

Astronomers had hoped to extend Swift's mission for a number of years by giving the satellite telescope a lift.

In July, Nasa and Arizona-based startup Katalyst launched a specially built rescue vehicle called LINK on a mission to rendezvous with Swift, latch onto the satellite and tug the observatory back into a higher, more sustainable orbit.

But the LINK spacecraft itself began spinning uncontrollably soon after reaching space, and by mid-August, mission managers abandoned the effort, resigned to letting Swift continue to meet its fate.

The aborted rescue attempt, the first US mission of its kind, took on heightened significance as a demonstration of a new orbital grappling technology seen as pivotal to the outcome of the US-China space race.

The LINK effort was closely watched as a trial run of a key satellite-maintenance technology with potential dual-use military space applications.

Katalyst touted the mission as a historic endeavour that designed, built and tested the LINK rescue vehicle on an unprecedented nine-month production schedule under a $30 million Nasa contract.

Swift was launched more than two decades ago to explore the most powerful known explosions in the universe, bursts of gamma-ray radiation emanating from the cores of distant galaxies.

Originally designed for a two-year prime mission, Swift remained in operation far longer with observations of a wide range of cosmic objects, from galaxies powered by supermassive black holes and stars emitting X-ray flares, to comets and asteroids streaking through our own solar system.

The aborted rescue attempt, the first US mission of its kind, took on heightened significance as a demonstration of a new orbital grappling technology seen as pivotal to the outcome of the US-China space race.
The LINK effort was closely watched as a trial run of a key satellite-maintenance technology with potential dual-use military space applications.
Katalyst touted the mission as a historic endeavour that designed, built and tested the LINK rescue vehicle on an unprecedented nine-month production schedule under a $30 million Nasa contract.
Swift was launched more than two decades ago to explore the most powerful known explosions in the universe, bursts of gamma-ray radiation emanating from the cores of distant galaxies.

Originally designed for a two-year prime mission, Swift remained in operation far longer with observations of a wide range of cosmic objects, from galaxies powered by supermassive black holes and stars emitting X-ray flares, to comets and asteroids streaking through our own solar system.

headline: NAB summons JUI-F chief's son over alleged irregularities in Pakistan Post appointments
subheadline: Asad Mahmood made appointments during his tenure as communications minister in 2022-23, says anti-graft body
author: Web Desk
article_text:
NAB directs JUI-F leader to appear before team on Nov 10.
NAB notice includes the use of fake and bogus documents.
FIA had also called former minister to record his statement.

The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has summoned former communications minister Asad Mahmood, son of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, over alleged irregularities in Pakistan Post Office appointments made during his tenure in 2022 and 2023.

Mahmood was appointed federal minister for communications in the coalition government led by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), following the ouster of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government through a no-confidence motion in April 2022.

The anti-corruption watchdog directed Mahmood to appear before its investigation team on November 10 at 11am to respond to questions concerning the recruitment process.

The investigation relates to alleged irregularities in appointments made at the Pakistan Post Office during his tenure as communications minister between 2022 and 2023.

According to the NAB notice, the Establishment Division had authorised recruitment against 3,938 vacancies in the Pakistan Post Office. However, 4,252 people were allegedly recruited, exceeding the approved number of positions.

The notice also alleges that appointments were made against 2,646 abolished vacancies in violation of the cabinet committee's instructions.

NAB further said that permanent appointments were made despite recommendations for recruitment on a contractual basis through a testing agency.

The allegations outlined in the notice also include the use of fake and bogus documents, recruitment of overage candidates and violations of the domicile quota.

The bureau warned that failure to comply with the summons could result in legal proceedings under Section 31 of the National Accountability Ordinance 1999.

Separately, the Federal Investigation Agency's (FIA) anti-corruption circle in Islamabad has also issued a summons to Mahmood in connection with the Pakistan Post recruitment investigation.

The FIA had directed the former minister to appear on November 2 at 11am to record his statement.

The agency is investigating alleged serious irregularities and corruption in recruitment at the Pakistan Post Office during Mahmood's tenure as the communications minister.

headline: Kylie Jenner seemingly gives Timothée Chalamet timeline to propose
subheadline: Kylie Jenner wants to win from Kendall Jenner as she puts Timothée under test
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kylie Jenner may have found herself in an unexpected race to the altar — and the competition reportedly involves her own sister, Kendall Jenner.

According to multiple outlet claims, Kylie is worried that Kendall's romance with Jacob Elordi could lead to an engagement before Timothée Chalamet puts a ring on her finger.

The situation has allegedly pushed the beauty mogul to demand a clearer commitment from her boyfriend of three years.

Read More: Timothee Chalamet's shocking role in Kylie Jenner surgery plans laid bare

"Kylie was the one who really pushed Kendall to go for Jacob, and it’s biting her in the butt," a source told Heat magazine.

"People are now saying they might end up engaged before she gets a ring on her finger, even though she and Timothée have been together so much longer, and it’s sent her into this weird competitive spiral."

The insider further alleges that Kylie has given Chalamet a deadline to make things official by the end of the year.

"She says she has to be first, and now she’s gone and given him an ultimatum. She says she wants some sort of proper commitment by the end of the year, or else."

But that strategy could create problems. The source claimed Chalamet is invested in the relationship but isn't ready to take that step just yet.

Kendall, meanwhile, has reportedly been telling people that Elordi is "husband material" and that their relationship is becoming increasingly serious.

Adding another twist, Chalamet has previously admitted that marriage is something he can imagine for himself.

Read More: Kylie Jenner celebrates 'forever sister' Kendall Jenner's 31st birthday

Asked about tying the knot, he teased, "Wow, that’s so personal. That’s so personal," before finally answering, "Yes."

Of course, these alleged sisterly wedding tensions remain unconfirmed.

headline: Democratic takeover of US Congress: What happens next
subheadline: Emboldened by victories, Democratic party is promising swift action on living costs and war in Iran
author: AFP
article_text:
Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees.

Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signalling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as "unprecedented corruption" in the government.

"Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they're not focused on making life better for the American people," he said.

But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation.

Here are the opportunities — and obstacles — ahead.

First 100 hours

Jeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House's first 100 hours, focused on affordability — the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war.

His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring.

With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to a vote and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns.

'Lawyer up'

Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump.

Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: "LAWYER UP."

Oregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: "Subpoenas."

With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.

Democrats have also signalled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.

Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party's numbers.

Senate muscle

The Senate majority gives Democrats another powerful lever: control of confirmations.

They can block Trump's judicial and cabinet nominees, including any selection to fill a Supreme Court vacancy, potentially curbing his influence over the courts long after he leaves office.

Democratic Senate chairs will also decide which bills and investigations receive committee attention.

Limits and deals

Passing laws will be much harder than launching investigations.

Most legislation must clear a 60-vote hurdle in the Senate to overcome procedural obstruction. Trump can veto bills passed by Congress, and overturning a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers.

He also retains substantial executive powers over immigration, trade and military operations, although lawmakers can seek to constrain them through legislation and spending decisions.

Trump struck a conciliatory note after the rout, praising Democrats for doing a "good job" and telling The New York Times that he would accept the result and expected to work with them.

He even raised the possibility of cooperation on immigration.

But he had previously warned that if Democrats won Congress, "I veto everything" — a reminder that the next two years could be defined as much by confrontation as compromise.

article_html:
Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees.

Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signalling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as "unprecedented corruption" in the government.

"Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they're not focused on making life better for the American people," he said.

But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation.

Here are the opportunities — and obstacles — ahead.

First 100 hours

Jeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House's first 100 hours, focused on affordability — the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war.

His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring.

With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to a vote and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns.

'Lawyer up'

Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump.

Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: "LAWYER UP."

Oregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: "Subpoenas."

With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.

Democrats have also signalled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.

Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate —  far beyond the party's numbers.

Senate muscle

The Senate majority gives Democrats another powerful lever: control of confirmations.

They can block Trump's judicial and cabinet nominees, including any selection to fill a Supreme Court vacancy, potentially curbing his influence over the courts long after he leaves office.

Democratic Senate chairs will also decide which bills and investigations receive committee attention.

Limits and deals

Passing laws will be much harder than launching investigations.

Most legislation must clear a 60-vote hurdle in the Senate to overcome procedural obstruction. Trump can veto bills passed by Congress, and overturning a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers.

He also retains substantial executive powers over immigration, trade and military operations, although lawmakers can seek to constrain them through legislation and spending decisions.

Trump struck a conciliatory note after the rout, praising Democrats for doing a "good job" and telling The New York Times that he would accept the result and expected to work with them.

He even raised the possibility of cooperation on immigration.

But he had previously warned that if Democrats won Congress, "I veto everything" —  a reminder that the next two years could be defined as much by confrontation as compromise.

headline: Sir Rod Stewart reveals surprising drinking habit ahead of farewell tour
subheadline: The 81-year-old singer will embark on his final arena tour, 'The Final Encore', next year.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sir Rod Stewart has revealed that his wife, Penny Lancaster, has placed restrictions on his drinking habits, as he loves to enjoy a glass of wine with his evening meal.

It is worth mentioning that the 81-year-old singer will embark on his final arena tour, The Final Encore, next year.

Ahead of his final time on the road, Rod revealed that he is making every possible effort to curb his drinking as his wife, Penny, 55, urged him to cut back on alcohol.

READ MORE: Rod Stewart shares reassuring health update following heart surgery

He told The Sun: 'I wish I could curb my drinking, but I love wine with an evening meal. I’ve got a great chef and I can’t drink water with a good meal.

'Penny says, "You must cut back, darling’" I only have a couple of glasses. But then, sometimes, I’ll get on the apple martinis and I can really knock those back.'

The music icon further revealed that he enjoys a rum and Coke after the third song, following an hour's workout, explaining that his strict exercise regime is part of his commitment to training 'like an athlete.'

headline: US federal court blocks Afghan deportation plan
subheadline: No "planned or confirmed chartered or commercial flights" to deport Afghan nationals, ICE official tells court
author: AFP
article_text:
Advocacy groups warn move could endanger former allies' lives.
Kabul voices "serious concern" over reported deportation plans.
UN has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings in Afghanistan.

WASHINGTON: A US federal court on Tuesday blocked the Trump administration's plans to deport scores of Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan, a move advocacy groups said could endanger their lives.

Judge Valerie Caproni of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York ruled that the United States could not send any Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan this week.

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Deputy Assistant Director Christopher George told the court there were "no planned or confirmed chartered or commercial flights" to deport Afghan nationals in the US to Afghanistan or Pakistan this week, according to court documents.

US media reported last week that more than 150 Afghans in the US would be deported via Pakistan to Afghanistan as part of President Donald Trump's latest immigration crackdown.

Among the group were relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies.

"A week ago, there was a plane. Today, the government told a federal judge there isn't one," AfghanEvac President Shawn VanDiver said in a statement after Tuesday's ruling.

"That didn't happen by accident. Veterans, advocates, 66 members of Congress, and thousands of Americans got this flight stopped," he added.

The Afghan Taliban regime voiced "serious concern" on Monday over the reported deportation plans.

Advocacy groups have warned that the removal of former allies and their families could endanger their lives.

After regaining power in 2021, the Afghan Taliban regime announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments and have repeated promises this year that their former foes could safely return home.

But the United Nations has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses.

Trump's administration last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown.

His administration sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the 2021 takeover by the Afghan Taliban regime.

headline: Prince William breaks silence amid Harry, Meghan 'unforgivable' act
subheadline: Future King William issues crucial video statement amid Thomas Markle letter claims
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William issued a video statement talking about the crucial next step amid reports that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle once again have gone behind the future King's back.

Kensington Palace released a video, showcasing the Prince of Wales applauding firefighters from South Wales Fire & Rescue Service and the Treherbert community who worked incredibly hard during UK wildfires.

William's team shared that Wales experiences around 60% of all UK wildfires, appreciating firefighters and other teams coming together to rescue and support the devastated community.

READ MORE: King Charles given security warning after police shock update

"A heartfelt thank you to everyone who worked tirelessly to keep people safe, and for sharing their experiences and lessons for the future," Palace said.

On the other hand, William expressed his immense gratitude towards firefighters for their "hell of an effort."

He added, "I was watching it, and I had loads of people talking to me about the fires through the summer and where they were on the news and watching it as well.

"It feels like this is what we are going to have to live with as a country as well as a world, now, I think; in most cases every summer, but being prepared and knowing what we're facing is going to be crucial.

"You guys did a hell of a job because you saved a lot of people’s houses, a lot of land, and I am thinking a lot of lives saved as well, so it was a gargantuan effort by all of you, so well done."

READ MORE: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle celebrate 'next chapter' in joint statement

Notably, this video message came after Tom Skye's shocking claim that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have been "attempting to drag" the Waleses into Thomas Markle's letter controversy.

headline: Lorraine Kelly confirms her show won't air Wednesday as ITV hit by studio issues
subheadline: 'Lorraine' has long been a regular presence on ITV’s morning broadcast since the programme launched in 2010
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lorraine Kelly’s talk show has been pulled from its regular slot on Wednesday, November 4, following a power outage at the studio where it is produced.

Lorraine typically airs on weekdays at 9:30 on ITV and ITV X, with Kelly as the host.

Early on Wednesday morning, the Scottish television personality took to her Instagram and shared a video post, updating fans that today’s episode won’t hit the airs.

“Hello there,” she says, “I’m on my way to work, but there’s been a little bit of a hoo-ha. There’s a power outage at the studio, so my show won’t by on today.”

However, she confirmed the viewers will still be able to catch Good Morning Britain, which airs on ITV preceding her show.

“So This Morning will still be on as well, just maybe a little bit later,” she added.

“So it’s a bit of a shame. I was really looking forward to talking to Sharleen Spiteri from the rock band Texas, but we shall reschedule, and it’ll all be fine. I will see you tomorrow.”

Lorraine has long been a regular presence on ITV’s morning broadcast since the programme launched in 2010.

headline: Blac Chyna hit with tax lien as child support deal makes headlines
subheadline: Rob Kardashian and Blac Chyna's child support history gets new attention
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Blac Chyna is facing a six-figure tax headache, with a new $116,732 lien filed against her in California for the 2024 tax year.

The development has also brought fresh attention to her past financial disputes with ex Rob Kardashian.

The reality star, whose legal name is Angela White, shares nine-year-old daughter Dream with Kardashian.

Read More: Blac Chyna, Rob Kardashian's warm co-parenting call sparks flirting talk

The former couple initially agreed to $20,000 in monthly child support after reaching a custody deal in 2017.

That arrangement didn't last. Kardashian later asked to reduce the payments, saying he could no longer afford them.

By March 2019, the pair had reached a new agreement: neither would pay child support, and they would share certain expenses, including medical and school costs.

Chyna once described raising her children without child support as her “biggest flex” during a 2020 interview.

“Just honestly taking care of my kids by myself as a single parent, but no child support,” she said.

But in 2022, she claimed she had been forced to give up three cars because she was a single mother receiving “no support.”

Kardashian disputed that account, saying he covered Dream's school tuition, medical bills and extracurricular activities.

Her co-parenting arrangement with rapper Tyga, with whom she shares son King Cairo, also involved shared custody without child support.

Chyna and Kardashian briefly sparked reconciliation rumours in October 2025 after she posted, “This love is forever,” and tagged him.

She later said they were “healing” and “just going with the flow.”

Read More: Blac Chyna celebrates ex Rob Kardashian's 39th birthday

However, by December, she had made her relationship status clear, declaring she was ending the year single.

Now, the tax lien has put Chyna's finances back in the spotlight.

headline: King Charles addresses viral rainy incident with witty remark
subheadline: King Charles did not shy away from uncomfortable topics from slavery reparations to tantrums during the storm
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles may have let his tantrums slip as the heavens opened up in a heavy downpour during his welcome in Antigua last week, but he proved there were no hard feelings for the rain.

The monarch, along with his wife Queen Camilla, concluded a nine-day royal tour of the Caribbean with a banquet for Commonwealth leaders in Antigua.

While delivering an emotional speech, the King seemed to have addressed the umbrella incident, which is now being dubbed as a ‘rain-gate’.

READ MORE: King Charles given security warning after police shock update

Speaking to the Commonwealth leaders in attendance, he emphasised that his role is to be an “umbrella for you all”.

Charles, who is the head of the Commonwealth, called the 84 dignitaries the “family of nations” one of the “world’s more improbable organisations”.

“It is one of the few organisations able to unite countries famous for snow, countries famous for deserts, and, most of all – countries whose citizens are utterly convinced they enjoy perfect weather all year round,” he said.

“Although perhaps part of my role as head of the Commonwealth is to provide an umbrella for you all!”

The witty joke was well received as laughter echoed through the hall and was followed by a round of applause.

The King also appeared pleased with himself and did not feel shy to crack a joke at his own expense.

headline: Meghan's mum Doria Ragland delivers delightful news to Archie, Lilibet
subheadline: Prince Archie, Princess Lilibet are set for big celebrations as Sussex family tries to move on from big storm
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are in for a special treat as their beloved grandmother Doria Ragland has big plans for the upcoming holiday season.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex, who relocated to the UK after six years in Montecito, are set to celebrate their first British Christmas with their children.

Prince Harry and Meghan have previously revealed that they prefer cosy and intimate festivities for Christmas.

READ MORE: George, Charlotte, Louis share festive tradition Archie, Lilibet return

They also revealed that they are setting their own family traditions for the holiday.

Meghan’s mum, Doria, is a huge part of their lives and sources have shared that the doting grandmother has been missing Archie and Lilibet a lot.

It is now revealed that rather than the Sussexes flying back to Montecito for the festivities, Doria will travelling across the pond.

Previously, reports claimed that since there was no expectation to have a Sandringham invitation from the royals, they would rather fly back. But HELLO! claims that the Sussexes are planning an early UK Christmas with Doria.

According to royal expert Emily Nash, Doria was “always the plan” in the Sussex celebration.

It is likely that Harry and Meghan wanted to be in the UK to mark some key events that are important to them.

It’s also expected that Harry and Meghan will mark the weekend's Remembrance events privately, and will not join the rest of the royal family at the Cenotaph in London.

READ MORE: Meghan Markle's befitting response to critics after ‘disgusting' attacks

headline: Wonderkid JJ Gabriel set to leave Man Utd for Real Madrid, reports suggest
subheadline: After Gabriel obtained a European passport, the way is not clear for him to ink a deal with any club outside England
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The 16-year-old prodigy, Man United forward JJ Gabriel, is reportedly inching closer to sealing the deal with Real Madrid.

Gabriel informed United he wanted to cancel his registration in order to become a free agent with immediate effect, in a notice posted on September 15, 2026.

Gabriel, who faced Altetico Madrid on United’s pre-season tour, had been expected to become the club’s youngest debutant in September’s Carabao Cup tie against Brighton.

However, he has chosen to look to elsewhere for senior football and has been training on his own while staying in Spain.

Europe’s leading clubs raced to select the United wonderkid after Gabriel travelled with his family to Barcelona in September.

Multiple UK media outlets reported at the time that Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Paris St-Germain are vying to sign JJ Gabriel, whose real name is Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel.

After Gabriel obtained a European passport, the way is not clear for him to ink a deal with any club outside England.

Gabriel scored two goals in his first two Premier League U-21 games for United this season but didn’t play against Brentford at Leigh Sports Village in September.

He was picked as the Premier League’s Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season kicked off.

headline: Sydney Sweeney's dream wedding could rival Taylor Swift's big day?
subheadline: The couple are also looking at places where they could get married
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sydney Sweeney and Scooter Braun are reportedly planning a wedding that can get everyone buzzing.

The couple have already started thinking about their big day and it seems like they want it to be something people will remember.

According to a source, Scooter is also hoping to make his proposal just as special but he has not yet decided how to ask Sydney to marry him.

Sydney, however, is said to know that a proposal is coming but she got no idea when it will happen. The source also claims that Scooter wants to give her a huge diamond ring and could spend at least $500,000 on it.

READ MORE: Is Sydney Sweeney the next James Bond girl?

The couple are also looking at places where they could get married. They have talked about having the wedding outside the US, but they are also considering Idaho.

The Housemaid actress spent some of her childhood there and the place is close to her extended family.

There is also another wedding that has caught Sydney's attention. She reportedly wants her big day to get the same love that Zendaya received after her private wedding to Tom Holland.

READ MORE: Sydney Sweeney gets close to Michele Morrone while filming 'The Housemaid 2'

Although Scooter is not said to be planning a wedding as big as Taylor Swift's, the couple reportedly want their celebration to be special enough to make headlines.

headline: Israel election commission rejects Netanyahu charges of fraud
subheadline: Election commission finds no evidence of irregularities after auditing 9,069 polling stations
author: AFP
article_text:
Electoral authorities dismiss allegations against Arab parties.
Netanyahu, Eisenkot lack majority to form government.
President Herzog to begin consultations with political parties.

Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

President Isaac Herzog will at noon (1000 GMT) officially receive the results of the October 27 election as he decides whether to give Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, with neither commanding enough votes alone.

The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results "accurately reflect the will of the voters".

"All complaints submitted by political factions have been reviewed and there were no findings indicating harm to the integrity of the election," it said in a statement.

Netanyahu has repeatedly alleged fraud by Arab-majority parties, pointing to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day and later saying lawmakers received money from Qatar — allegations that have been levelled at his own aides in the past.

Late on Tuesday, Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would not question anyone without evidence after reports that the head of the domestic security service Shin Bet, a Netanyahu ally, had asked to interrogate Arab parties.

Netanyahu's Likud party lashed out at her, saying that she was trying to "obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors".

Eisenkot, a former military chief trying to unite centrists and the centre-right and turn the page on Netanyahu's long, polarising reign, accused Likud of attempting a "pogrom against democracy".

He had earlier warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

No unity government

Lapid, a former prime minister and key force in the opposition bloc, pointed to the midterm elections in the United States in which Democrats resoundingly trounced Trump's Republicans.

The Shin Bet "outbursts" paired with the US election results "eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu".

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a "broad national government" — with himself at the top.

Herzog's statements have raised speculation that he could sound out leaders on a possible unity government, hoping to bring stability in a country sharply split after three years of war and over Netanyahu's hard-right politics.

Herzog holds a largely ceremonial role as head of state, but carries the decisive vote on who will have the first chance to try to be prime minister — a process that could last weeks or even months and may end in failure and new elections.

After officially receiving the results, Herzog begins two days of consultations with parties, starting with the smaller ones.

Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot holds the 61 seats needed to secure a majority in the 120-member parliament.

Netanyahu's bloc has an edge, with 53 seats as opposed to Eisenkot's 48.

Eisenkot could reach the threshold if he were to ally with parties from the Arab minority, whose seat count surged to 19 on outrage against the actions and rhetoric of Netanyahu's government.

But some in the opposition have baulked at relying on non-Jewish lawmakers' votes.

'Fresh thinking'

Herzog, a mild-mannered lawyer whose political career was in the defunct left-wing Labour Party but is now officially nonpartisan, has said he wants to encourage "fresh thinking" and avoid a new election.

Once Herzog tasks someone, they will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.

If no one succeeds, Herzog will give the mandate to someone else. If that too fails, a majority of lawmakers could come together to nominate someone within 21 days — or else Israel heads to new elections.

It took Netanyahu, who at the time had a better showing by Likud, 58 days to form a government after the last election in November 2022.

Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022 after repeated deadlocks.

Netanyahu faces corruption charges and the risk of jail if he loses power and, with it, immunity.

Yousef Jabareen, the head of the largest Arab-majority party in the next parliament, told AFP this week that the opposition needed to accept "political reality" and team up to remove Netanyahu.

Netanyahu has persistently warned Jewish Israelis that the opposition will work with Arab parties, which he accuses of backing Hamas.

headline: KATSEYE explains last-minute cancellation of Detroit concert amid backlash
subheadline: Megan Skiendiel's illness results in last-minute cancellation of KATSEYE's 'Wildworld Tour' Detroit concert
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Katseye is apologising to the Eyekons after leaving thousands of fans disappointed with a last-minute concert cancellation.

The iconic girl group issued a statement to their Instagram Stories, explaining that they were forced to postpone their Wildworld Tour concert in Detroit on Tuesday, November 3, due to bandmember Megan Skiendiel falling ill.

“Unfortunately, Megan is unwell and unable to perform tonight, and we want to make sure she has the time she needs to rest and recover,” they revealed, adding, “We know so many of you have traveled, made plans, and been looking forward to tonight. We are disappointed that we won’t get to see you, and we’re truly sorry for the inconvenience.”

READ MORE: KATSETE celebrates their big AMAs win with tribute to Taylor Swift, BTS

“Thank you for your patience, understanding, and for always showing us so much love. We love you and can’t wait to see you soon,” the statement concluded.

Fans who were already present at the venue shared videos of the message that flashed on stage: “We’re sorry to share that the KATSEYE show scheduled for tonight at Little Caesars Arena has been postponed due to illness. If you’re already at the venue, please follow instructions from venue staff.”

One concertgoer, Alliz Nguyen, revealed that VIP ticket holders got to see the band perform a sound check and join them for photo ops. However, the concert itself was cancelled about half an hour prior to starting.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ailiz Nguyen | UGC & Content Creator (@ailiztnguyen)

Eyekons had noticed Megan was not feeling well during their last concert in Hamilton on November 1. Despite their sympathies, a majority of the fans expressed their disappointment with Katseye, noting that they could have at least announced the cancellation earlier.

With Megan under the weather, only two of the six girls, Daniela Avanzini, Lara Raj, and Yoonchae Jeung remain. Frotwoman Sophia Laforteza will return from her hiatus and join the girls on the road in January, while Manon Bannerman’s hiatus remains indefinite.

READ MORE: KATSEYE announces Sophia's return after brief mental health hiatus

headline: Judi Dench reveals in memoir that Daniel Craig pushed to kill off M in 'Skyfall'
subheadline: 'Apparently, it was Daniel’s idea to have me killed' Dench reveals in her upcoming memoir, 'Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It?'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Dame Judi Dench, who starred as 007’s boss M in eight James Bond movies over two decades, reveals that Daniel Craig was behind M’s death in 2012’s Skyfall.

Dench recalled how she came to know that her character M would be killed off in her upcoming memoir, Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It?, an excerpt of which appeared in Variety.

“I was taken to the Wolseley restaurant by Barbara, Michael and Sam (Mendes, the director)—I don’t think Daniel Craig was there—and they outlined the plot and told me they were going to bump me off. My fault, I suppose,” Dench said.

“Ever since GoldenEye, when the entire film unit went off to Monte Carlo and St. Petersburg and I only had three days in Watford, I’d been begging them to let me out from behind my desk,” she continued.

“Well, they did finally let me out from behind my desk…and they shot me.”

“Apparently, it was Daniel’s idea to have me killed. But first I had to suffer the indignity of being sacked by Ralph Fiennes. Arsehole (laughs),” Dench quipped.

Dench, who first took on the role in 1995’s GoldenEye opposite Pierce, then revealed that the decision had been made to kill off her character.

headline: Sarah Ferguson 'revives' career on Instagram as public outings spark fear
subheadline: Beatrice and Eugenie's mother takes key step to rebuild image after confirming UK return
author: Areeba Khan
article_text:
Sarah Ferguson is said to be planning to rebuild her career and image with the help of social media. This way, the former Duchess can easily maintain distance from the public eye amid fears of harsh encounters.

On October 29, Fergie finally confirmed her return to the UK with an unexpected public appearance alongside Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie.

The former Duchess of York attended the memorial service for her former boyfriend and longtime pal Paddy McNally in London.

READ MORE: Sarah Ferguson breaks silence after UK return: 'In contact with Andrew'

Dressed in a blue lacy coat, Sarah appeared in good spirits after months in hiding as a result of her involvement in the Epstein files.

Now, as she returns, an insider said that Andrew's ex-wife is planning her comeback via Instagram.

Sarah's last post was made on September 11, 2025. She remembered the victims of the tragic 9/11 attack.

"My thoughts and prayers are with the families who lost loved ones, the survivors, and the first responders whose bravery and selflessness remind us of the very best of humanity. We must never forget," King Charles' former sister-in-law wrote at the time.

Since then, Sarah has been quiet, as back-to-back charities she has been associated with dropped her due to her 'past' ties with paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

However, she has now returned with a plan. A source shared that Sarah Ferguson might begin sharing her side of the story via an emotional social media post.

Earlier, People reported that Fergie is lying low as she is resettling in the UK.

READ MORE: Beatrice, Eugenie forced to take difficult step before Andrew's crucial testimony

"She’s happy spending time with her family and focusing on her relocation. She is embracing her family life and seeing her grandchildren," Sarah's spokesperson shared.

headline: Why is ‘This Morning' pre-recorded today? Lorraine Kelly breaks silence
subheadline: ITV daytime shows pulled off air after studio power cut
author: Web Desk
article_text:
ITV’s daytime schedule was disrupted on Wednesday, November 4, after a power outage at the studio, which forced both This Morning and Lorraine off air.

Lorraine Kelly, 66, announced the news in an Instagram video filmed on her way to work.

She told fans: “There’s been a little bit of a hoo-ha. There’s a power outage at the studio, so my show won’t be on today.”

She explained that Good Morning Britain had still aired and that technicians hoped to resolve the issue by around 11:00 a.m., but confirmed her planned interview with Texas frontwoman Sharleen Spiteri would be rescheduled.

She added: “It’s a bit of a shame. These things happen. Can’t be helped. See you tomorrow.”

Both This Morning and Loose Women were then canceled, and a repeat of the show took place in their stead, as well as a Tipping Point: Best Ever Finals in the 12.30 pm timeslot. Regular programming was anticipated to resume at 2 pm after ITV's Lunchtime News.

This failure occurred amid growing discussions regarding the power situation in the UK and fears that the shortage of gas that can power the plants may cause further blackouts.

Lorraine has been on ITV's schedule since 2010; however, last year its airing time was decreased from one hour to just half an hour for just 30 weeks a year due to budget cuts, an adjustment Kelly found heartbreaking until she admitted that it "really worked out well."

Kelly stated that she will be back on TV tomorrow at 9.30 am.

headline: Kate Siegel reveals one pop star she would love to see on screen
subheadline: Kate Siegel dreams of working with this one musician on a film
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kate Siegel, one of the most renowned names in the horror cinema, believes that music "unlocks" stories which is why she builds her movies around a record.

The 44-year-old director and actress revealed that one of her favourite contemporary musician is Olivia Rodrigo, who she would also like to see on the screen.

In her interview, the Hush star noted, "One of my dream goals is to cast Olivia Rodrigo in something, because I just think she's such a good actress, like, inside, and the way she presents it outside. And I just love the way she exists. And I remember thinking, like, remember when artists used to write albums for movies? Wouldn't it be great? Oh, and she's so perfect."

The interviewer also agreed with Siegel, adding, "Like, she's my favourite of that, you know, of that style and stature right now. Just because, I mean, she's so tapped in to, and talks about all the time, you know, what she was raised on with her parents, and Weezer and Radiohead, and The Cure, and all of that stuff. And it's like, oh man, what she's, the Handmaid's Tale song that she just put out."

The Haunting of Hill House actress then recalled how she first became a fan, saying, "Do you know? No, she's so into it. I remember the same girlfriends that I talked to about Episode 3, when Sour came out. One of my friends, Mara, sent it to me, and she's like, you have to listen to this. This is what high school felt like. And it was crazy to see that 20 plus years later, it was. It was, well, 25, 27."

READ MORE: Check out list of A-stars directing new horror anthology

The Fall of the House of Usher actress continued, "Yeah, it was just right there. It's fu--ing, it's always brutal out there. You know what I mean? Oh yeah, no, to get her, someone like her to do it, like you said, like the whole, like Queen to Highlander, you know, how they did, that's the one that comes to mind."

Siegel then called out to Rodrigo, saying, "We're just putting it out there. Olivia! Somebody, can somebody like tag, do the thing that people do, tell her that I like her. Tag it, tag it."

Later in the interview, the filmmaker updated on her current project in the works, which she is writing as well as directing.

Siegel noted that she has not gotten to the casting yet, and added, "So we're out there. Olivia Rodrigo. Call me."

headline: Govt announces decision on abolishing Rs10 banknote
subheadline: Federal cabinet approves replacing Rs10 banknote with coin, alongside new currency designs
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal cabinet has approved replacing the Rs10 banknote with a coin of the same denomination, marking a major policy decision months after the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) dismissed reports of its discontinuation.

The decision was taken on the recommendation of the Ministry of Finance during a cabinet meeting that also approved designs for a new series of currency notes.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister's Office, the cabinet received a detailed briefing on the proposed designs, which were developed after seeking suggestions from artists and designers across the country.

A cabinet committee constituted by the prime minister also held extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders before the designs were presented for approval.

The meeting was informed that the new currency notes would incorporate enhanced security features to prevent counterfeiting.

Modern materials would also be used to improve the durability and lifespan of the banknotes.

SBP had earlier dismissed discontinuation reports

The decision comes after the central bank rejected social media reports in September suggesting that the Rs10 banknote was being discontinued and that a deadline had been set for exchanging existing notes.

At the time, the SBP described the reports as baseless, saying a proposal for a new banknote series was under consideration by the federal cabinet and no decision had been taken on replacing or discontinuing any denomination.

The central bank had also clarified that any decision regarding the withdrawal of banknotes would be formally communicated to the public, with adequate time provided for exchanging discontinued currency.

Earlier, SBP Deputy Governor Dr Inayat Hussain had informed the Senate Standing Committee on Finance that the central bank was considering discontinuing the Rs10 banknote because of its rising production cost.

He had also disclosed that the SBP had made two previous attempts to discontinue the denomination.

The latest cabinet decision does not specify when the Rs10 banknote will cease to be legal tender or provide a deadline for exchanging existing notes.

headline: Dylan Sprouse exposes how little he earned from Disney hit
subheadline: The show first came out in 2005 and ended in 2008
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Dylan Sprouse has shared a surprising story about his time on Disney Channel and the amount he received has left many people shocked.

The actor spent years playing Zack Martin in The Suite Life of Zack and Cody but he says the only extra payment he remembers getting from the show was just five cents.

Dylan spoke about this on his Wildmen podcast, where he was joined by his former co-star Phill Lewis.

The two actors looked back at their days on the show and talked about what happened behind the scenes.

READ MORE: Dylan Sprouse uncovers shocking family history after becoming a dad

During their chat, Dylan explained that the five cent payment came from a special episode that also featured characters from Hannah Montana. Even though The Suite Life was a big hit and was shown in many countries, he says he never received another payment like that.

The show, however, first came out in 2005 and ended in 2008. Its next series The Suite Life on Deck continued until 2011.

Both shows together got around 190 episodes.

READ MORE: Sydney Sweeney's dream wedding could rival Taylor Swift's big day?

Phill also spoke about how Disney dealt with actors' pay at the time. But the conversation was not only about money. Dylan praised Phill for always being there for him and called him a second father figure.

headline: Lorry driver electrocuted after truck hit 11,000-volt overhead power line
subheadline: Andy Lloyd, 56, was pronounced dead at the spot in Tany Dderwen Farm in Betws-yu-Rhos, Conwy, on May 1, 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A tripper lorry driver, Andy Lloyd, 56, was transporting a load of hardcore to a farm when the grab arm on his truck struck overhead power cables.

The moment Lloyd stepped out of the cab of his truck while his teenage son sat alongside him, he hit the 11,000-volt power lines; an inquest in Ruthin was heard.

Ruthin Coroner’s Court heard Lloyd from Bod Elian, LIanelian in Conwy, jumped out of the cab and was electrocuted when he made contact with the metal step.

Lloyd was pronounced dead at the spot in Tan y Dderwen Farm in Betws-yu-Rhos, Conwy, on May 1, 2026.

The court heard that Lloyd’s son, whose identity has not been disclosed to respect the privacy, had joined his father in the lorry that unfortunate day to try his hand at work.

Senior coroner John Gittins for North Wales East and Central read from the teenager's statement.

According to the teenager’s testimony read in the coroner’s court, it reveals that Lloyd had moved the lorry closer to where contractors were putting up a shed and where the load was meant to be dumped when the grab arm hit the power cables.

It added that the teenager tried to warn his father of the danger ahead, but Lloyd had already exited the cab.

One of the onlookers rescued the teenager in the lorry and helped him exit safely.

The coroner concluded that the lorry driver Lloyd died as a consequence of an accident.

Ruthin Coroner’s Court heard Lloyd from Bod Elian, LIanelian in Conwy, jumped out of the cab and was electrocuted when he made contact with the metal step.
Lloyd was pronounced dead at the spot in Tan y Dderwen Farm in Betws-yu-Rhos, Conwy, on May 1, 2026.
The court heard that Lloyd’s son, whose identity has not been disclosed to respect the privacy, had joined his father in the lorry that unfortunate day to try his hand at work.
Senior coroner John Gittins for North Wales East and Central read from the teenager's statement.

According to the teenager’s testimony read in the coroner’s court, it reveals that Lloyd had moved the lorry closer to where contractors were putting up a shed and where the load was meant to be dumped when the grab arm hit the power cables.
It added that the teenager tried to warn his father of the danger ahead, but Lloyd had already exited the cab.
One of the onlookers rescued the teenager in the lorry and helped him exit safely.
The coroner concluded that the lorry driver Lloyd died as a consequence of an accident.

headline: John Frieda's cause of death: Celebrity hairdresser dies aged 75
subheadline: John Frieda, celebrity hairstylist and Frizz-Ease creator dies
author: Web Desk
article_text:
John Frieda, the celebrity hairstylist behind the bestselling Frizz-Ease hair care line, has died at the age of 75, his salon announced on Instagram.

The official statement reads: “It is with heavy hearts that we share the news that our dear John passed away peacefully, surrounded by his family. John was more than a mentor to us; he was a true icon of the hair industry.”

Alan Howard Frieda was born in 1951 in London. Like his father and grandfather, he chose a career in hairdressing and was employed at Leonard Lewis's House of Leonard salon.

His name was changed from Alan to John because of another stylist who shared the same name in the salon.

In addition to working for British Vogue and Harper's Bazaar magazines, he founded his own first salon in New Cavendish Street in 1976 and invented an unusual haircut named Purdey for Joanna Lumley from The New Avengers.

His clients included not only Twiggy, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, and Princess Diana but also Madonna, Nicole Kidman, and Scarlett Johansson. He got married to the famous Scottish singer Lulu in 1977; however, after 14 years, he divorced her. In 2019, he married Avery Agnelli, a widow of one of Fiat's heirs.

In the 1990s, Frieda stopped cutting hair and devoted himself entirely to building a product empire.

His Frizz-Ease, which he introduced in 1988, became one of the world's top moneymakers, and in 2002 he, together with his business partner Gail Federici, sold the company to the Japanese corporation Kao for $450 million.

Tributes poured in, with model Jo Wood recalling that Frieda did her hair when she was 16, and Cetera Lamb, creative director of his London salon, calling him “a true legend, a real maverick in hairdressing.”
