subheadline: Sean 'Diddy' Combs is celebrating his 57th birthday behind bars at FCI Allenwood Low
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sean “Diddy” Combs is marking another birthday behind bars, and one of the first in line to wish him was his longtime nemesis 50 Cent.

The In Da Club rapper trolled the disgraced music mogul with a sarcastic Instagram birthday wish on Wednesday, November 4. Sharing a picture of Combs with greying hair and beard, Fiddy wrote, “Happy 57th B day Diddy wishing you many more, LOL.”

Instead of the lavish celebrations he once enjoyed, Combs is spending his birthday serving his 50-month prison sentence. However, according to Us Weekly, the music mogul will receive a special birthday menu at FCI Allenwood Low, where he was transferred from FCI Fort Dix in October.

READ MORE: Diddy gets shifted to new prison over 'safety' concerns

The move came after Combs reportedly sustained a head injury and was taken to a hospital. Claims that he had been involved in a prison fight with fellow inmate Christopher “Dudus” Coke, a Jamaican drug lord, were denied by the Bureau of Prisons.

According to Us Weekly, Combs started his birthday with oatmeal, scrambled eggs, fruit, whole wheat bread with jelly, and whole milk. Lunch options include a hamburger or black bean burger with oven-browned potatoes, while dinner features pork roast, mashed potatoes with gravy, and mixed vegetables.

Combs was arrested in September 2024 and sentenced in October 2025 after being convicted on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. His current release date is February 6, 2028.

headline: Obama's 'Kennedy' remark fuels Jon Ossoff 2028 presidential buzz after Georgia victory
subheadline: Obama highlighted Ossoff's connection to late civil rights leader John Lewis
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff's victory in Georgia's midterm elections has reignited speculation about his presidential ambitions, with former President Barack Obama's recent praise and the 39-year-old's growing online popularity drawing fresh attention.

Ossoff defeated Republican Representative Mike Collins, who was backed by President Donald Trump, on Tuesday, November 3, securing another six-year term in a state Trump won during the 2024 presidential election.

However, much of the attention surrounding his victory has shifted towards the 2028 presidential race, with political commentators and supporters drawing comparisons between Ossoff and Obama.

Speaking at an election rally on October 28, Obama praised the Georgia senator and joked that "he looks like a Kennedy, all handsome in the videos."

The former president also highlighted Ossoff's connection to late civil rights leader John Lewis, who mentored both politicians.

Meanwhile, Ossoff has gained an unusual following on social media, where videos of his speeches and photographs of his increasingly muscular appearance have attracted attention.

Some supporters have even described him as "jacked", while his confrontational speeches against Trump have circulated widely online.

His popularity has also caught the attention of political analysts. CNN's Kasie Hunt suggested that his election victory marked the beginning of a possible presidential campaign, according to the Daily Mail.

Despite the speculation, Ossoff has repeatedly rejected suggestions that he intends to seek the White House.

During an October debate, he said he had "zero interest" in running for president and promised to complete his six-year Senate term if re-elected.

Ossoff first entered the Senate in 2021 after winning a closely watched Georgia runoff election.

His latest victory has strengthened his national profile, although he has made no announcement suggesting that he plans to enter the 2028 presidential race.

headline: LEGO releases its largest-ever set with over 12,000 pieces, $800 price tag
subheadline: LEGO's previous record holder set was the World Map with 11,695 pieces
author: Web Desk
article_text:
LEGO has launched its biggest construction set to date, with over 12,000 pieces and a retail price almost $800, providing fans with the challenge of building one of the world's most iconic architectural structures.

The Danish toy manufacturer has unveiled its new collection of 12,060 pieces that will allow builders to create a small version of the iconic basilica in Barcelona, Spain and will be available on November 1.

The model is $799.99 in the U.S., £649.99 in the U.K. and €749.99 throughout Europe.

The finished product contains detailed towers, elaborate facades and colourful stained glass windows to look like those in the original building.

The set also portrays the process of the basilica's construction starting from its crypt and gradually adding the facades, interior sections and towers.

The latest release is the company's largest set in terms of number of pieces, with 12,060 pieces, compared to the previous record holder, the World Map with 11,695 pieces.

The launch coincides with the 100th death anniversary of Antoni Gaudí, the Spanish architect who dedicated much of his career to designing the Sagrada Família.

Construction of the real basilica began in 1882, and despite more than a century of work, some decorative elements remain unfinished.

LEGO designer Rok Zgalin Kobe described recreating the landmark as a challenging task because of its architectural complexity.

The company first unveiled the set in June 2026 before making it available for purchase worldwide this month.

Designed primarily for adults, the model is part of LEGO's Architecture collection, which features miniature versions of famous buildings and landmarks.

headline: Cardi B recalls 'uncertain' pregnancy as son with ex Stefon Diggs turns 1
subheadline: The rapper was going through a tumultuous divorce with Offset when she welcomed her first child with Diggs
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Cardi B is opening up about the difficult circumstances surrounding her fourth pregnancy as she and Stefon Diggs celebrate their son’s first birthday.

On Wednesday, November 4, the Grammy-winning rapper shared an emotional tribute on Instagram, revealing her baby boy’s name publicly for the first time while reflecting on the challenges she faced while carrying him.

“Happy 1st birthday to Grey Marsean Diggs,” Cardi wrote. “It’s only been 1 year since meeting you but it feels like I’ve had you at my side forever.”

READ MORE: Stefon Diggs shares where he stands in relationship with Cardi B

The mother of four went on to describe how her son helped her navigate an especially difficult period in her life.

“I carried you through one of the most uncertain and high pressured times of my life but having you inside of me through it all gave me a extra strength,” she wrote. “I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life! You gave a new meaning to what a Grey day feels like. You light up my life and every room with your smile your laugh and your precious spirit.”

Cardi, 34, first confirmed she’s dating Stefon, 32, in December 2024 after months of speculation. By September of next year, she announced that they are expecting their first child together — her fourth overall (Cardi shares three kids with ex-husband Offset).

During her pregnancy, Cardi was going through a tumultuous divorce with Offset, and the pair famously took multiple jabs at each other on social media.

In February, the Bodack Yellow hitmaker confirmed that she had broken up with Stefon. A source told US Weekly that the pair broke up a few days before the Super Bowl LX because he allegedly “betrayed her so many times.”

Despite their breakup, Cardi and Diggs have continued to co-parent their son and have been spotted together on multiple occasions.

article_html:
Cardi B is opening up about the difficult circumstances surrounding her fourth pregnancy as she and Stefon Diggs celebrate their son’s first birthday.

On Wednesday, November 4, the Grammy-winning rapper shared an emotional tribute on Instagram, revealing her baby boy’s name publicly for the first time while reflecting on the challenges she faced while carrying him.

“Happy 1st birthday to Grey Marsean Diggs,” Cardi wrote. “It’s only been 1 year since meeting you but it feels like I’ve had you at my side forever.”

READ MORE: Stefon Diggs shares where he stands in relationship with Cardi B

The mother of four went on to describe how her son helped her navigate an especially difficult period in her life.

“I carried you through one of the most uncertain and high pressured times of my life but having you inside of me through it all gave me a extra strength,” she wrote. “I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life! You gave a new meaning to what a Grey day feels like. You light up my life and every room with your smile your laugh and your precious spirit.”

Cardi, 34, first confirmed she’s dating Stefon, 32, in December 2024 after months of speculation. By September of next year, she announced that they are expecting their first child together — her fourth overall (Cardi shares three kids with ex-husband Offset).

During her pregnancy, Cardi was going through a tumultuous divorce with Offset, and the pair famously took multiple jabs at each other on social media. 

In February, the Bodack Yellow hitmaker confirmed that she had broken up with Stefon. A source told US Weekly that the pair broke up a few days before the Super Bowl LX because he allegedly “betrayed her so many times.”

Despite their breakup, Cardi and Diggs have continued to co-parent their son and have been spotted together on multiple occasions.

headline: Iran's supreme leader threatens wider war if US resumes strikes
subheadline: Iran's chief negotiator says American voters rejected war during the midterm elections
author: AFP
article_text:
Khamenei says Trump's election setback will not change US policy on Iran now.
Trump says US forces remain ready to strike targets inside Iran if needed.
Tehran says diplomacy remains possible as mediators work to prevent fighting.

TEHRAN: Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump.

Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress.

The results could constrain Trump's ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes.

"Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement Wednesday.

He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating.

Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages.

Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he posted on X.

"If the US government betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf said.

Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been "defeated both militarily and politically".

The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war.

Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done," Trump told Fox News.

On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession.

"They built an anti-aircraft facility... As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely," Trump told US media, but he called it a "minor attack".

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a US MQ-1 drone was "intercepted and destroyed" over Qeshm Island. There was no confirmation from the US side.

Locked and loaded

Earlier this week the president said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," he said. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."

The president's remarks come with diplomatic efforts by mediators in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.

On Tuesday Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Pezeshkian said Iran's supreme leader had granted the government new powers to negotiate on issues previously off-limits.

Qatar, a mediator in the protracted wrangling, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal.

Both sides "are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented", Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters.

China also said Wednesday that avoiding a return to hostilities was a top priority in its diplomatic efforts with the countries.

The war, triggered in February when the US and Israel pummelled Iran in a massive wave of strikes, has been at a stalemate for months.

Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if Washington resumes the war.

He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating.

"If the US government betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf said.

Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been "defeated both militarily and politically".

The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war.

Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done," Trump told Fox News.

On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession.

"They built an anti-aircraft facility... As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely," Trump told US media, but he called it a "minor attack".

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a US MQ-1 drone was "intercepted and destroyed" over Qeshm Island. There was no confirmation from the US side.

Locked and loaded

Earlier this week the president said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," he said. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."

On Tuesday Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Pezeshkian said Iran's supreme leader had granted the government new powers to negotiate on issues previously off-limits.

Qatar, a mediator in the protracted wrangling, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal.

Both sides "are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented", Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters.

China also said Wednesday that avoiding a return to hostilities was a top priority in its diplomatic efforts with the countries.

The war, triggered in February when the US and Israel pummelled Iran in a massive wave of strikes, has been at a stalemate for months.

Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if Washington resumes the war.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he posted on X.
"If the US government betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf said.
Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been "defeated both militarily and politically".
The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war.
Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.
"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done," Trump told Fox News.
On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession.
"They built an anti-aircraft facility... As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely," Trump told US media, but he called it a "minor attack".
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a US MQ-1 drone was "intercepted and destroyed" over Qeshm Island. There was no confirmation from the US side.
Locked and loaded

Earlier this week the president said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.
However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary.
"We seem to be getting everything we want," he said. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."
The president's remarks come with diplomatic efforts by mediators in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.
On Tuesday Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.
Pezeshkian said Iran's supreme leader had granted the government new powers to negotiate on issues previously off-limits.
Qatar, a mediator in the protracted wrangling, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal.
Both sides "are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented", Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters.
China also said Wednesday that avoiding a return to hostilities was a top priority in its diplomatic efforts with the countries.
The war, triggered in February when the US and Israel pummelled Iran in a massive wave of strikes, has been at a stalemate for months.
Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if Washington resumes the war.

headline: Cynthia Erivo joins Snoop Dogg biopic as mother of this legend
subheadline: 'Wicked' star Cynthia Erivo cast as Tupac’s mother in Snoop Dogg biopic
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Cynthia Erivo has joined the cast of Snoop, the upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic, where she will play Afeni Shakur, the mother of Tupac Shakur.

The film is directed by Craig Brewer, with Outer Banks star Jonathan Daviss taking the title role as the rap icon.

Afeni Shakur is described as a fascinating figure in her own right.

Read more: Snoop Dogg breaks silence on near death experience

A former Black Panther activist, she had a profound impact on her son, the late rapper Tupac Shakur. Her life was explored in the recent FX documentary Dear Mama, which has helped keep her story in the spotlight.

The casting continues a run of real-life roles for Erivo.

She has recently played Aretha Franklin and Harriet Tubman in biopics, and she starred in both Wicked films, a part that has made her one of the best-known performers on screen today.

Erivo is now in demand for stories rooted in real history, and the role of Afeni brings together two major figures in hip-hop’s story.

Afeni’s relationship with Tupac is central to how many fans understand him, and her inclusion suggests the film will touch on the wider world around Snoop Dogg’s rise.

The film’s other cast members, writer and production timeline have not yet been detailed.

Read more: Cynthia Erivo reveals where she stands with Ariana Grande

headline: 'Texas is not for sale': Talarico sends message to Elon Musk after historic election win
subheadline: Musk contributed $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund in September
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Democratic Senator-elect James Talarico has sent a strong message to billionaire Elon Musk after defeating his preferred candidate in Texas, declaring that the state is not for sale despite more than $150 million being spent to prevent his victory.

Talarico defeated Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in Tuesday's (November 3) midterm elections, becoming the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat from Texas since 1988.

Speaking to CBS News on Wednesday, Talarico said the election results showed that even the world's wealthiest individuals could not simply buy political influence.

"The people of Texas delivered a crystal-clear message to the world's first trillionaire: Texas is not for sale," he said.

The remarks were aimed at Musk, who contributed $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund in September. The Republican-aligned political group subsequently transferred the money to a committee supporting Paxton's campaign.

Musk's trust also donated another $10 million to a separate political committee working to elect Paxton.

Talarico accused the Tesla CEO of attempting to secure political influence over Texas, particularly over land, water and resources needed for his expanding data centre operations.

He alleged that Musk wanted a senator who would serve his business interests, although the billionaire has not publicly acknowledged any such arrangement.

Meanwhile, Musk reacted sarcastically to the Republican defeats on X, writing: "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time."

He also posted that space-based data centres were looking increasingly attractive.

The Texas result was part of a broader Democratic victory that saw Gina Hinojosa defeat Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending more than three decades of Republican control of the state's governorship.
